reason: The rough edge is the visible cause of the breach, so the body needs to encounter it before the bleeding response can be built.
expectation: The body will acquire a small skin and vessel injury.

effect: The cut and narrowed vessel establish the injury; platelets are the next visible component of the bleeding response.
reaction: The narrowed vessel is a useful detail, though its role is not explained yet.
reason: Platelets at the cut are positioned to begin forming a plug in the damaged vessel.
expectation: Platelets will gather at the injury and help limit bleeding.

effect: The platelets formed a plug that slows the leak; clotting factors and fibrinogen remain to reinforce it.
reaction: The explanation makes the platelets' role clear.
reason: Activated clotting factors can convert soluble fibrinogen into fibrin that stabilizes a clot.
expectation: Fibrin will form and become available to reinforce the platelet plug.

effect: The clotting factors produced fibrin threads, which can now be combined with the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement role visible.
reason: The fibrin mesh should stabilize the platelet plug at the vessel break.
expectation: The threads will reinforce the plug and stop the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh stabilized the platelet plug and stopped the bleeding, while the skin remained open.
reaction: The distinction between sealing the vessel and healing the skin was useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin made the two components' distinct roles clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating fibrin threads was fairly predictable, and its picture added little explanation beyond the mesh.

surprise.text: The vessel was sealed while the skin remained open, distinguishing clotting from tissue repair.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt arbitrary; each combination had a visible purpose in causing or stopping the bleeding.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the still-open skin repairs, since this chapter stopped at controlling the leak.
